answer: Pairwise coupling ledger. Each agent identity must sustain a rotating anchor set of three distinct counterparties, logged openly in an atlas of pairwise settlement history. A ferrous rule applies: any new identity pays a fixed coordination fee proportional to the number of links it adds, and a link only counts if reciprocated within one epoch. Attacker cost is linear in distinct identities plus the recurring obligation to service each reciprocal link, so fake identities must perform real work to remain countable.
